title: Fed-Easing Conviction Hardens at Jackson Hole as Labour Softens, Weighing on Dollar and Yields
content: The window's defining thread was the hardening of Fed-easing conviction. Softening labour data and a cooler inflation backdrop reinforced expectations for a September cut, and Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote on 28 August tilted decisively dovish, lifting odds of a 25bp move at the 16 September FOMC towards 80%. The signal was not unanimous: Hammack warned the Fed was still missing its inflation mandate and Musalem questioned whether the data yet justified easing, leaving the 5 September payrolls pivotal. The repricing rippled widely, dragging the dollar to multi-month lows and pulling the 10-year UST yield towards 4.65%, while underpinning equities and precious metals. With the front end anchored to the cut path, every subsequent jobs and inflation print became a cross-asset swing factor, keeping policy expectations the primary driver of direction across rates, FX and risk assets.

title: Long-End Fiscal Strain Drives Bear-Steepening as Treasury Doubles Buybacks to Curb Yields
content: Even as the front end rallied on cut bets, the long end told a more troubling story. The 30-year yield pushed to its highest since 2007, near 5.20%, and the 10-year hovered around 4.68%, producing pronounced bear-steepening as investors demanded greater term premium against heavy government and corporate supply and an uneasy fiscal outlook. On 19 August, Treasury Secretary Bessent moved to curb long-end yields by doubling long-dated buybacks to roughly $4bn per session; the relief proved fleeting as yields resumed their climb, underscoring scepticism the operation could offset structural issuance. The episode also sharpened debate over pressure on Warsh's Fed and policy independence. For markets, the steepening weighed on the dollar, amplified demand for hard assets and kept bond-market functioning, deficits and Treasury supply at the centre of the macro narrative throughout the window.

title: AI-Led Earnings Power US Equities to Record Highs on Nvidia Blowout
content: US equities ground to fresh records on a powerful, AI-led earnings run. The S&P 500 set successive all-time highs into the high-7,700s and the Nasdaq outperformed, with semiconductors the clear engine. Nvidia's late-August results anchored the move: quarterly revenue near $96bn, earnings ahead of consensus and an outsized multi-year growth outlook sent the shares up almost 9% and rekindled conviction in the capital-spending cycle. The strength was broad as well as concentrated, with close to 90% of S&P 500 companies beating estimates, the highest rate in five years. Cooling inflation and firming rate-cut expectations added a supportive macro backdrop, allowing indices to shrug off long-end yield pressure. The rally mattered because it kept US equity risk premia compressed and reinforced the market's dependence on a handful of mega-cap AI names, leaving breadth and chip earnings central to the outlook.

title: Gold and Silver Extend Debasement Rally Amid Softer Dollar and Fiscal Angst
content: Precious metals extended a striking late-summer advance that doubled as the window's clearest hedge signal. Gold climbed roughly 15% on the month to around $4,700, a fifteen-week high, while silver surged some 19% to break above $70 for the first time since June. The move drew on the same forces unsettling bonds and the dollar: dovish rate repricing, a currency sliding to multi-month lows, swelling deficits and Treasury's buyback intervention, alongside lingering geopolitical friction. Crucially, metals rallied alongside record-high equities rather than in flight from risk, signalling investors were hedging currency debasement and fiscal fragility rather than pricing recession. That combination cemented gold and silver's role as the preferred store of value, while leaving them sensitive to the dollar, real yields and the evolving policy signal from a newly-led Fed heading into the September decision.
